旅行活动：一份骑行说明的完整语境

正式GT考试样题用于活动信息理解，不是分级读物；规则、收费、协助方式都在完整原文中。

集体骑行：时间安排、规则和援助

以下为正式样题原始材料。先按原题要求作答，再看原答案与对应解释；材料描述的是原文中的语境，不把历史数据当作当前事实。

原材料 · 第1页

Read the text below and answer Questions 1-8.

London to Brighton Bike Ride

The start The bike ride starts at Clapham Common tube station. • Your Start Time is indicated by the colour of your body number in this pack. It is also printed on the address label of the envelope. Please arrive no earlier than 30 minutes before that time. • We allocate an equal number of cyclists for each Start Time to ensure a steady flow. Please keep to the time you've been given so we can keep to our schedule and avoid delaying other riders and prevent 'bunching' further down the route. • An Information Point, toilets and refreshment stands will be open from very early in the day.

Ride carefully We put together as many facilities as possible to help ensure you have a troublefree day. But we also rely on you to ride safely and with due consideration for other cyclists and road users. Although many roads are closed to oncoming traffic, this is not always the case and you should be aware of the possibility that there could be vehicles coming in the opposite direction. Please do not attempt reckless overtaking whilst riding – remember it is NOT a race.

Follow all instructions Every effort is made to ensure that the route is well signed and marshalled. Please obey all directions from police and marshals on the route. If you hear a motorcycle marshal blow his/her whistle three times, move left.

Wear a helmet Every year we are delighted to see more riders wearing protective helmets, but we would like to see every cyclist on the ride wearing one. More than half of reported injuries in cycling accidents are to the head, and a helmet gives the best protection when the head hits the ground.

Attracting assistance If you have an accident, ask a marshal for help; they are in contact with the support/emergency services. To call for help from our motorcycle marshals, give a 'thumbs down' signal. The marshal will do all he/she can to help, providing he/she is not already going to a more serious accident. If a motorcycle marshal slows down to help you, but you have just stopped for a rest and don't need help, please give a 'thumbs up' signal and he/she will carry on. Remember – thumbs down means 'I need help'.

原材料 · 第2页

In case of breakdown Refer to your route map and make your way to a Mechanics Point. Mechanical assistance is free when you show your Rider Identity Card; you just pay for the parts.

Refreshment stops Look out for these along the route. Most are organised by voluntary clubs and their prices give you real value for money. They are also raising money for their local communities and the British Heart Foundation, so please give them your support.

Rain or shine – be prepared In the event of very bad weather, watch out for signs to wet weather stations en route. Good waterproofs, like a cycle cape, are essential. Our first aid staff can only supply bin liners and by the time you get one you may be very wet. However, the English summer is unpredictable – it may also be hot, so don't forget the sun protection cream as well!

If you have to drop out We will try to pick up your bike for you on the day. Call Bike Events (01225 310859) no more than two weeks after the ride to arrange collection. Sorry, we cannot guarantee this service nor can we accept liability for any loss or damage to your bike. Bike Events will hold your bike for three months, after which it may be disposed of. You will be charged for all costs incurred in returning your cycle.

人工智能：承诺、实施条件与制度风险

先读这一组完整原文页，再完成对应原题。以下时代、数量与观点均按考试文章语境理解。

原文 · 印刷页46

READING PASSAGE 3

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 27-40, which are based on Passage 3 below.

Artificial Intelligence

In many countries in the West, hysteria about the future of artificial intelligence (AI) is everywhere. There seems to be no shortage of sensationalist news about how AI could cure diseases, accelerate human innovation and improve human creativity. Just looking at the media headlines, you might think that we are already living in a future where AI has infiltrated every aspect of society.

While it is undeniable that AI has opened up a wealth of promising opportunities, it has also led to the emergence of a mindset that can be best described as 'AI solutionism'. This is the philosophy that, given enough data, machine learning algorithms can solve all of humanity's problems. But, in fact, instead of supporting AI progress, this mindset actually jeopardises the value of machine intelligence by disregarding important AI safety principles and setting unrealistic expectations about what AI can really do for humanity.

In only a few years, AI solutionism has made its way from the technology evangelists' mouths in Silicon Valley in California to the minds of government officials and policymakers around the world. The pendulum has swung from the dystopian notion that AI will destroy humanity to the utopian belief that our algorithmic saviour is here.

We are now seeing governments pledge support to national AI initiatives and compete in a technological race to dominate the burgeoning machine-learning sector. While many politicians proclaim the transformative effects of the coming 'AI revolution', they fail to realise the complexity around deploying advanced machine learning systems in the real world.

One of the most promising varieties of AI technologies are neural networks. This form of machine learning is loosely modelled on the neuronal structure of the human brain, but on a much smaller scale. But what many politicians do not understand is that simply adding a neural network to a problem will not automatically mean that you'll find a solution. Similarly, adding a neural network to a system of government does not mean it will be instantaneously more inclusive or fair.

AI systems need a lot of data to function, but the public sector typically does not have the appropriate data infrastructure to support advanced machine learning. Most of the data remains stored in offline archives. The few digitised sources of data that exist tend to be buried in bureaucracy. More often than not, data is spread across different government departments that each require special permissions to be accessed. Above all, the public sector typically lacks the human talent with the right technological capabilities to fully reap the benefits of machine intelligence.

For these reasons, the sensationalism over AI has attracted many critics. Stuart Russell, a professor of computer science at the University of California, Berkeley, has long advocated a more sensible and realistic approach that focuses on simple everyday applications of AI instead of the

原文 · 印刷页47

hypothetical takeover by super-intelligent robots. Similarly, Rodney Brooks, professor of robotics at Massachusetts Institute of Technology, writes that 'almost all innovations in robotics and AI take far, far, longer to be really widely deployed than people in the field and outside the field imagine'.

One of the many difficulties in deploying machine learning systems is that AI is extremely susceptible to adversarial attacks. This means that a malicious AI can target another AI to make it behave in a certain way, such as forcing it to make wrong predictions. Many researchers have warned against the rolling out of AI without appropriate security standards and defence mechanisms. Still, AI security remains an often overlooked topic when machine learning systems are installed.

If we are to reap the benefits and minimise the potential harms of AI, we must start thinking about how machine learning can be meaningfully applied to specific areas of government, business and society. This means we need to have a discussion about AI ethics and the distrust that many people have towards machine learning.

Most importantly, we need to be aware of the limitations of AI and where people still need to take the lead. Instead of painting an unrealistic picture of the power of AI, it is important to take a step back and separate the actual technological capabilities of AI from fantasy.

The medical profession has also recognised the drawbacks to AI. The IBM Watson for Oncology programme was a piece of AI that was meant to help doctors treat cancer. Even though it was developed to deliver the best recommendations, human experts found it hard to trust the machine. As a result, the AI programme was abandoned in most hospitals where it was trialled.

Similar difficulties arose in the legal domain when algorithms were used in courts in the US to sentence criminals. An algorithm calculated risk assessment scores and advised judges on the sentencing. The system was found to amplify structural racial discrimination and was later abandoned.

There are some crucial lessons here for everyone aiming to boost investments in national AI programmes. These examples demonstrate that there is no AI solution for everything. Using AI simply for the sake of AI may not always be productive or useful, and not every issue is best addressed by applying machine intelligence to it. All solutions come with a cost and not everything that can be automated should be.

阅读 · 海洋资源：捕捞与鱼群恢复

根据短文和给定情境作答。

A fish stock can be assessed in two different ways: the rate at which fish are removed and the size of the remaining population. Excessive harvesting is described as overfishing; a population that is too small is described as overfished. Managers use scientific assessments to set catch limits and plan recovery. Monitoring and enforcement help ensure that fishing actually follows these limits.

What causes overfishing, and what measures could prevent it?

哪一句可以由短文支持？

  • A A population immediately recovers once fishing is within an acceptable rate.
  • B The rate of fishing and the size of the fish population describe the same thing.
  • C Setting a catch limit is not the same as ensuring that boats comply with it.
  • D A small fish population proves that the current fishing rate is excessive.
答案

C。设定捕捞上限与确保实际遵守是两件事。

The Davies Sisters｜印象派转向与战时收藏未作答笔记填空 / 事实判断 TFNG · 3 段 · 268 词 · 4 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 18 页

原文与作答 · 分开滚动

原文第5段However, it was only a few years before their collecting took a new direction and they turned to the work of the French Impressionists***. We know that Hugh Blaker, as a champion of contemporary French art had a hand in the decision, and we know also that they would have seen examples on their various trips to Paris. Whatever the precise reason for this change, their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice by the French artist Claude Monet. Over the next 12 years, the sisters amassed the bulk of their Impressionist collection, including six further works by Monet, two more by Manet, and three by Renoir, including his well-known painting La Parisienne.

原文第6段The First World War (1914-1918) played a part in the development of the sisters' collection. Their initial response to the war effort was to finance the safe passage of artists from occupied Belgium to Wales, as a humanitarian act, but also with the hope of establishing a vibrant artists' community in the area. Later in the conflict, both sisters decided to volunteer at a canteen for troops at Troyes, in northern France; Gwendoline in 1916, followed by Margaret in 1917.

原文第7段It was tedious and distressing work, which would have a permanent effect on Gwendoline's health. Yet on one of numerous trips to nearby Paris, she visited the Bernheim-Jeune Gallery. Here she acquired two works by Cézanne - Provençal Landscape and The François Zola Dam. The paintings were shipped directly to Bath, England, where they became the first works by Cézanne to go on display in a public gallery in Britain.

*** Impressionist: an artist with a style of painting that developed in France in the late 1800s by Renoir, including his well-known painting La Parisienne

原页文字提示：脚注引文保留原页；其后半句涉及 Renoir 作品，属于来源编辑瑕疵，不要把整条脚注当作英语完整定义范例。这里的 Impressionist 指印象派画家。

题目与作答

Q5–6：Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage. Q10–11：TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN。

5. the first Impressionist paintings they bought showed places in 5 __________

6. they worked in a 6 __________ for soldiers in France

10. Hugh Blaker opposed the Davies sisters' decision to buy art by French Impressionists.

11. The exhibition of Cézanne paintings at the Bath gallery was very popular with the public.

对照答案，回到证据

第 5 题 · Venice

题干问画中的地点，不是买画地点；Paris是干扰信息。

their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice

第 6 题 · canteen

soldiers对应troops；a后填地点canteen，不能答城市Troyes。

both sisters decided to volunteer at a canteen for troops at Troyes

第 10 题 · FALSE

champion与had a hand in说明支持并参与，和opposed相反，属于明确反证。

Hugh Blaker, as a champion of contemporary French art had a hand in the decision

第 11 题 · NOT GIVEN

原文只确认首次公开展出，没有观众反响或人数。全文也未提供其受欢迎程度；first与popular不可互换。

the first works by Cézanne to go on display in a public gallery in Britain

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

姐妹的收藏逐渐转向法国印象派。文章承认影响因素存在，却没有把转向归结为一个已确定的原因；随后把战争中的救助、志愿服务和购画经历交织起来，展示私人行动如何最终进入公共文化生活。

原文第5段

However, it was only a few years before their collecting took a new direction and they turned to the work of the French Impressionists***. We know that Hugh Blaker, as a champion of contemporary French art had a hand in the decision, and we know also that they would have seen examples on their various trips to Paris. Whatever the precise reason for this change, their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice by the French artist Claude Monet. Over the next 12 years, the sisters amassed the bulk of their Impressionist collection, including six further works by Monet, two more by Manet, and three by Renoir, including his well-known painting La Parisienne.

收藏方向改变后，姐妹开始购入法国印象派作品。支持当代法国艺术的Hugh Blaker参与了这个决定，她们在巴黎旅行时也应当接触过相关作品，但作者没有断言某一个因素就是决定性原因。1912年她们购入莫奈的威尼斯风景，之后12年形成了印象派收藏的主体。the bulk强调大部分藏品在这一时期积累。

原文第6段

The First World War (1914-1918) played a part in the development of the sisters' collection. Their initial response to the war effort was to finance the safe passage of artists from occupied Belgium to Wales, as a humanitarian act, but also with the hope of establishing a vibrant artists' community in the area. Later in the conflict, both sisters decided to volunteer at a canteen for troops at Troyes, in northern France; Gwendoline in 1916, followed by Margaret in 1917.

第一次世界大战也影响了她们的收藏经历。她们起初出钱帮助被占领比利时的艺术家安全来到威尔士，这既出于人道关怀，也带有发展当地艺术家社群的愿望。后来两人先后到法国为部队食堂做志愿服务。本段把文化理想放在战争救助的现实行动中，而不是只讲艺术市场。

原文第7段

It was tedious and distressing work, which would have a permanent effect on Gwendoline's health. Yet on one of numerous trips to nearby Paris, she visited the Bernheim-Jeune Gallery. Here she acquired two works by Cézanne - Provençal Landscape and The François Zola Dam. The paintings were shipped directly to Bath, England, where they became the first works by Cézanne to go on display in a public gallery in Britain.

食堂工作单调又令人痛苦，并对格温多琳的健康产生了持久影响。即使如此，她仍在赴巴黎期间参观画廊并购买塞尚的两幅画。这些作品被直接运往英国巴斯，成为英国公共画廊首次展出的塞尚作品。最后一句将个人购藏的故事转向公众能够接触艺术的变化。

词语与搭配

took a new direction

转向新的方向

主语可以是事业、研究或活动的发展；这里的collecting指持续的收藏实践发生变化。

had a hand in the decision

参与或影响了这个决定

have a hand in不表示独自决定；文中同时承认旅行见闻等可能影响。

a vibrant artists' community

一个充满活力的艺术家社群

vibrant强调活跃、有创造力；artists'是复数所有格，community指艺术家相互联系形成的群体，不只是建筑或展馆。

go on display in a public gallery

开始在公共画廊展出

go on display强调从未展出到展出的状态变化，public gallery使私人收藏与公共接触联系起来。

句子精读

Whatever the precise reason for this change, their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice by the French artist Claude Monet.

无论这一变化的确切原因是什么，她们于1912年10月首次购入的印象派作品，都是法国画家克洛德·莫奈描绘威尼斯的风景画。

Whatever the precise reason是省略了may have been一类成分的让步结构，表示不论原因如何。主干是their first purchases were scenes of Venice；made in October 1912是过去分词短语，补充购入时间；by...说明作者。this change指收藏转向印象派，日期、描绘对象与作者属于不同层面的信息。

Their initial response to the war effort was to finance the safe passage of artists from occupied Belgium to Wales, as a humanitarian act, but also with the hope of establishing a vibrant artists' community in the area.

她们最初对战时行动的回应，是资助艺术家从被占领的比利时安全前往威尔士；这是一项人道行动，同时也寄托着在当地建立活跃艺术家社群的希望。

主干是Their initial response was to finance...，不定式说明具体行动。from...to...标明迁移起止地。as a humanitarian act与with the hope of...并列说明两层动机，but also在这里补充文化愿景而非否定人道目的。the area指威尔士当地；hope表明愿望，不能直接当成已经实现的结果。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

a vibrant artists' community

一个充满活力的艺术家社群

适合与support、sustain、help build搭配，讨论实体文化空间如何为创作者提供交流和演出机会。这里借用表达描述一种可能作用，不把文中救助艺术家的历史直接当成剧院效果的证据。

Why we need silence｜漂浮舱的两项实验未作答摘要填空 / 人物／特征匹配 · 3 段 · 311 词 · 5 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

原文与作答 · 分开滚动

DResearchers are also seeking to understand what aspects of silent experiences are most beneficial to our health. One of the best-researched is the flotation tank: a lightproof, soundproof tank of salt water in which a person floats as a form of deep relaxation. While some people experience altered perception in the tanks, involving subtle humming sounds and visual effects, these effects are benign and do not detract from the benefits of the experience, says Justin Feinstein, a clinical neuropsychologist. 'When you don't have external sensory stimuli coming in, the brain tries to fill the void to make sense of this dark and silent world,' he explains. 'In these tanks, some people can even hear the sound of their eyes blinking,' says Feinstein. 'But it is the ability to focus on the breath that helps people reach a relaxed or meditative state.'

E（第一段）E To further explore flotation tanks as a therapeutic tool, Feinstein and his colleagues recruited 50 people with a variety of conditions related to stress and had them answer a questionnaire prior to and following a flotation session. Participants reported decreases in muscle tension, pain and symptoms of their conditions after a single, 1-hour float, alongside an increase in feelings of relaxation and overall wellbeing.

E（第二段）Less is known about what effects sensory deprivation can have on the brain. To investigate, Feinstein's team had 48 people participate in either three 90-minute float sessions or three 90-minute periods of relaxing on a chair which reclined. Participants had their brains scanned using functional magnetic resonance imaging at the beginning and end of the trial. Float sessions uniquely decreased activity in the default mode network (DMN), a collection of brain regions commonly linked with depression. Feinstein says it is an exciting finding, because flotation tanks seem to offer a way of 'resetting' our nervous system to prevent it from getting out of balance.

  • B Justin Feinstein
  • C Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan
  • D Eric Pfeifer

这一部分围绕漂浮舱提出两个层次的问题：人主观上有什么感受，脑活动发生了什么变化。文章分别介绍问卷与脑扫描研究，并保留科学解释中的不确定性；参与者报告的轻松感不能直接扩大成对所有疾病或所有人的疗效结论。

D

D Researchers are also seeking to understand what aspects of silent experiences are most beneficial to our health. One of the best-researched is the flotation tank: a lightproof, soundproof tank of salt water in which a person floats as a form of deep relaxation. While some people experience altered perception in the tanks, involving subtle humming sounds and visual effects, these effects are benign and do not detract from the benefits of the experience, says Justin Feinstein, a clinical neuropsychologist. 'When you don't have external sensory stimuli coming in, the brain tries to fill the void to make sense of this dark and silent world,' he explains. 'In these tanks, some people can even hear the sound of their eyes blinking,' says Feinstein. 'But it is the ability to focus on the breath that helps people reach a relaxed or meditative state.'

漂浮舱通过遮光、隔音和盐水漂浮减少外界感觉输入。有人会听见轻微嗡鸣或出现视觉感受，Feinstein认为这可能是大脑在缺少外界刺激时尝试填补空白。这些现象在他的描述中是良性的；真正帮助进入放松状态的，是把注意力放在呼吸上的能力。本段是在介绍一种体验及专家解释，并非要求读者自行进行治疗。

E（第一段）

E To further explore flotation tanks as a therapeutic tool, Feinstein and his colleagues recruited 50 people with a variety of conditions related to stress and had them answer a questionnaire prior to and following a flotation session. Participants reported decreases in muscle tension, pain and symptoms of their conditions after a single, 1-hour float, alongside an increase in feelings of relaxation and overall wellbeing.

研究团队招募50名有不同压力相关状况的人，在一次漂浮前后填写问卷。参与者报告一小时后肌肉紧张、疼痛和相关症状减少，放松感与整体舒适感提高。这里的信息来自参与者的前后自报；本段没有交代对照条件或长期追踪，因而只宜理解为此次研究中观察到的短时体验变化。

E（第二段）

Less is known about what effects sensory deprivation can have on the brain. To investigate, Feinstein's team had 48 people participate in either three 90-minute float sessions or three 90-minute periods of relaxing on a chair which reclined. Participants had their brains scanned using functional magnetic resonance imaging at the beginning and end of the trial. Float sessions uniquely decreased activity in the default mode network (DMN), a collection of brain regions commonly linked with depression. Feinstein says it is an exciting finding, because flotation tanks seem to offer a way of 'resetting' our nervous system to prevent it from getting out of balance.

第二项研究改为考察大脑：48人分别接受三次90分钟漂浮或在躺椅上放松，并在研究开始和结束时做功能磁共振扫描。原文报告只有漂浮组出现默认模式网络活动降低，该网络常与抑郁有关。Feinstein把这解释为可能帮助神经系统重获平衡的线索；seem和resetting上的引号提醒读者，这是一种试探性、形象化解释，不等于已经证明能治疗抑郁。

外界感觉刺激

stimuli是stimulus的复数，指来自声音、光线等的感觉输入；这里解释漂浮舱改变了什么环境条件。

do not detract from the benefits

detract from后接价值、效果或吸引力，表示使其减少；文中是专家对特定体验的评价。

作为一种治疗或辅助治疗手段

as标明研究考察的用途，therapeutic不意味着已经获得对所有疾病的有效性证明。

prior to与following平行标明两个测量时点；它们本身并不说明因果或效果能维持多久。

句子精读

Why we need silence｜主动安静与短时收益未作答段落信息匹配 / 人物／特征匹配 · 3 段 · 304 词 · 4 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

原文与作答 · 分开滚动

F（第一段）F Neurobiologist Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan is also an advocate of silence as a therapy. 'When we find ways to be quiet, we are not only quiet in our environment, but quiet in our inner selves,' she explains. 'This allows us to be more aware of what is happening around us and what the situation may require from us so we can provide [a more] adequate response.'

F（第二段）Not everyone will benefit from silence to the same extent, but Ben-Soussan says one characteristic is key: the person must need to want to engage in the experience. 'We see from animal models and human studies that volition and intentionality is important,' she says. 'When people do not want silence, it can be very distressing.'

GEric Pfeifer, a psychotherapy researcher, also concedes that some people may not benefit from silence, particularly those who are in a heightened state of stress. 'People in these states may not be able to relax or calm down in a silent condition,' he says. Professional guidance can be useful, he adds, allowing people to approach silence slowly so that they can gradually enjoy the benefits. And Pfeifer is convinced that silence is more attainable in everyday life than people think. First, complete silence isn't necessary. In a recent study, he found that participants reported more relaxation and less boredom when they sat quietly in an outdoor garden compared with a completely silent room. Second, Pfeifer believes we don't need a lot of silence to gain benefits. 'You don't need to spend hours in silence,' he says. 'It is likely better to have more frequency of silence for a few minutes at a time than a longer period of silence only once a week. Just finding those places in your daily life where you can find some silence ... can make a big difference.'

材料精读 · 内容与词句

安静在这里不是越彻底、越久就越好。文章强调个人意愿、当前心理状态和适应过程，再把理想化的绝对无声，转化为日常中较容易获得的短暂安静。

F（第一段）

F Neurobiologist Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan is also an advocate of silence as a therapy. 'When we find ways to be quiet, we are not only quiet in our environment, but quiet in our inner selves,' she explains. 'This allows us to be more aware of what is happening around us and what the situation may require from us so we can provide [a more] adequate response.'

Ben-Soussan把安静区分为外部环境的安静与内在状态的安静。她认为后者可以帮助人更清楚地觉察周围情况，并作出合宜反应。This承接这种内外安静的状态，而不是单指没有任何声音；本段呈现的是她对安静作用的解释。

F（第二段）

Not everyone will benefit from silence to the same extent, but Ben-Soussan says one characteristic is key: the person must need to want to engage in the experience. 'We see from animal models and human studies that volition and intentionality is important,' she says. 'When people do not want silence, it can be very distressing.'

文章马上加入限制：不同人的获益程度不一样，而且主动愿意参与体验很重要。volition与intentionality指个人的意愿和有意识的参与。如果一个人并不想处于安静之中，这种情境反而可能令人痛苦。因此，安静不能被当成不顾意愿、对所有人都适用的要求。

G

G Eric Pfeifer, a psychotherapy researcher, also concedes that some people may not benefit from silence, particularly those who are in a heightened state of stress. 'People in these states may not be able to relax or calm down in a silent condition,' he says. Professional guidance can be useful, he adds, allowing people to approach silence slowly so that they can gradually enjoy the benefits. And Pfeifer is convinced that silence is more attainable in everyday life than people think. First, complete silence isn't necessary. In a recent study, he found that participants reported more relaxation and less boredom when they sat quietly in an outdoor garden compared with a completely silent room. Second, Pfeifer believes we don't need a lot of silence to gain benefits. 'You don't need to spend hours in silence,' he says. 'It is likely better to have more frequency of silence for a few minutes at a time than a longer period of silence only once a week. Just finding those places in your daily life where you can find some silence ... can make a big difference.'

Pfeifer进一步指出，高度紧张的人有时无法在安静环境中放松，专业指导可以帮助其逐渐适应。他随后提出两个让安静更可获得的想法：不必绝对无声，研究参与者在安静花园中比完全无声的房间更放松、较少无聊；也不必每次持续很久。他倾向于频繁短时的安静，但原文用likely表达判断，并未给出对所有人有效的固定时长处方。

to the same extent

达到相同程度

用于比较程度；Not everyone...to the same extent表示人与人之间有差异，不是所有人完全没有益处。

engage in the experience

参与并投入这种体验

engage in后接活动或过程；此处强调主动愿意参与，而不只是身体置于安静房间。

a heightened state of stress

一种压力升高、紧张加剧的状态

heightened修饰state所指的程度，描述当时状态，不能直接给某人贴上永久性标签。

a few minutes at a time

每次几分钟

at a time说明单次持续长度，与一周只进行一次但时间很长相对照。

句子精读

Professional guidance can be useful, he adds, allowing people to approach silence slowly so that they can gradually enjoy the benefits.

他补充说，专业指导可能有所帮助，让人慢慢接近和适应安静，从而逐渐享受到其中的益处。

he adds是插入的转述语，he指Pfeifer。allowing...补充说明专业指导如何起作用；so that连接渐进适应与预期收益。can be useful表示可能有帮助，slowly与gradually共同强调过程，而非立即强迫人进入完全无声的状态。

In a recent study, he found that participants reported more relaxation and less boredom when they sat quietly in an outdoor garden compared with a completely silent room.

在近期的一项研究中，他发现参与者报告说，相比待在完全无声的房间里，安静地坐在室外花园中会让他们更放松，也更少感到无聊。

found后的that从句说明研究发现，reported提醒这是参与者报告的体验。when从句描述花园条件，compared with引出对比的房间条件。more relaxation与less boredom是两个并列变化；recent以原文写作时点为参照，句子没有宣称花园对每个人或每种健康状况都更有效。

原文与作答 · 分开滚动

原文第1段Ulbe Bosma's The World of Sugar is a genuinely global history. Bosma discusses all the sugar growing places of the world, beginning with Cuba and Java, the largest exporters of the early 20th century. But this is a history not just of cane sugar but also of beet sugar, an equally important form of traded sugar over the last hundred years. Beet sugar is grown mainly in Europe and the United States. It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.

原文第2段Bosma's discussion of the sugar market in Britain gives a sense of the book's range. The sweet-toothed British first bought cane sugar from their own slavery-dependent colonial plantations. Following the abolition of slavery in the British Empire, cane sugar was imported to Britain from places which retained the practice, such as Cuba and Brazil. Towards the end of the 19th century, the British started to import beet sugar from continental Europe. Only in the 20th century was there a move to develop a national beet sugar industry.

原文第3段The book provides a global labour history, investigating the wide range of labour regimes associated with growing sugar. Contrary to popular belief, cane sugar production was never just restricted to large, dedicated plantations owned by rich men. For example, in Java, a huge exporter of sugar in the early 20th century, sugar cane was grown together with rice in an extraordinarily labour-intensive way by small farmers.

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

这是一篇书评的开头：作者介绍Bosma如何把糖写成一部全球贸易史和劳动史。甘蔗糖与甜菜糖、进口来源的变化、大种植园与小农生产相互补充，使糖的历史不再只剩单一地区或单一劳动制度。

原文第1段

Ulbe Bosma's The World of Sugar is a genuinely global history. Bosma discusses all the sugar growing places of the world, beginning with Cuba and Java, the largest exporters of the early 20th century. But this is a history not just of cane sugar but also of beet sugar, an equally important form of traded sugar over the last hundred years. Beet sugar is grown mainly in Europe and the United States. It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.

书评首先评价这是一部真正具有全球范围的糖史，既讨论古巴和爪哇等甘蔗糖出口地，也把欧洲、美国的甜菜糖纳入。随后指出补贴与人为压低的价格会影响世界市场，威胁甘蔗糖生产者的生计。It指甜菜糖这一行业和产品，不能理解为世界上所有糖生产都采用同一制度。

原文第2段

Bosma's discussion of the sugar market in Britain gives a sense of the book's range. The sweet-toothed British first bought cane sugar from their own slavery-dependent colonial plantations. Following the abolition of slavery in the British Empire, cane sugar was imported to Britain from places which retained the practice, such as Cuba and Brazil. Towards the end of the 19th century, the British started to import beet sugar from continental Europe. Only in the 20th century was there a move to develop a national beet sugar industry.

英国市场的进口变化展示了全书的跨度：先从依赖奴役劳动的本国殖民种植园购买甘蔗糖，废奴后仍从保留奴隶制的古巴、巴西等地进口，19世纪末开始进口欧洲甜菜糖，20世纪才发展本国甜菜糖业。这段揭示，某国法律改变与商品供应链中的劳动制度变化并不一定同步。

原文第3段

The book provides a global labour history, investigating the wide range of labour regimes associated with growing sugar. Contrary to popular belief, cane sugar production was never just restricted to large, dedicated plantations owned by rich men. For example, in Java, a huge exporter of sugar in the early 20th century, sugar cane was grown together with rice in an extraordinarily labour-intensive way by small farmers.

作者转向劳动组织的多样性，纠正甘蔗糖始终只由富人拥有的大型专门种植园生产这一单一想象。爪哇的小农曾以高度劳动密集的方式同时种甘蔗和水稻，是这种多样性的一个实例。not just restricted强调不只存在大种植园，并没有否认大种植园的重要历史。

词语与搭配

sold at artificially low prices

以人为压低的价格出售

artificially在这里指价格受到补贴等外部干预，不是说产品是假货；at引出出售价格。

threatening the livelihood of

威胁……的生计

livelihood指赖以谋生的方式和收入基础；此处现在分词说明低价竞争带来的影响。

Following the abolition of slavery

在奴隶制废除之后

following相当于after，标记时间关系；它本身不保证其他国家或供应链也同时发生同样变化。

Contrary to popular belief

与普遍看法相反

用于引入与常见理解不一致的事实，后面需要具体内容或例证支持，不能只把自己的意见写成事实纠正。

an extraordinarily labour-intensive way

一种极为依赖大量劳动投入的方式

labour-intensive描述生产对劳动投入的依赖程度，与单纯技术先进或落后不是同一个概念。

句子精读

It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.

甜菜糖还获得了巨额补贴，并在世界市场上以人为压低的价格出售，威胁着甘蔗糖生产者的生计。

It承接上句的beet sugar；has been统领subsidised和sold两个被动分词。at引出价格，on world markets说明交易范围。末尾threatening...是补充结果的现在分词短语，说明受影响的是甘蔗糖生产者，而非把两种糖当成同一种生产群体。

For example, in Java, a huge exporter of sugar in the early 20th century, sugar cane was grown together with rice in an extraordinarily labour-intensive way by small farmers.

例如，在20世纪初的重要食糖出口地爪哇，小农以极其劳动密集的方式，把甘蔗与水稻一起种植。

主干是sugar cane was grown...by small farmers。a huge exporter...是Java的同位语，交代地区背景；together with rice说明共同种植的作物，in...way说明生产方式。句子把出口规模大与生产者是小农放在一起，说明两者可以同时成立。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

threatening the livelihood of

威胁……的生计

适合用于描述资源衰退或不公平竞争怎样影响依赖某产业谋生的人。可以作为结果分词短语，但要让前面的原因具体可理解。

用于写作：现有题目明确谈过度捕捞对数百万人生计的风险；表达可直接连接鱼类资源减少与沿海家庭收入受损。
